intro_html: Creamy beef stroganoff turned into a make-ahead skillet that fits your macros. Each bowl carries 52 grams of protein for around $4.61 (at everyday cost) and the batch makes 14 servings. This is the kind of stick-to-your-ribs dinner that usually costs a lot more away from home.
cost_closing_html: About $4.61 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Every one of the 14 servings delivers 52 grams of protein and 601 calories, so this creamy classic still earns its spot on a lean plan.
upsell_html: Rich, creamy, and ready in the fridge all week. Comfort food does not have to break the budget. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: White mushrooms cost less than baby bellas and cook down the same, so grab the cheaper carton.
Light sour cream gives you the classic creamy tang with less fat, and one tub covers the whole batch.
Stir the sour cream in off the heat so it does not curdle. A small technique tip that saves you from wasting a good ingredient.
make_it: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion and a pat of butter, then drain.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and shrink down.
Boil the rotini separately until just tender, then drain.
Pour in the beef broth and dijon, simmer, then stir in the light sour cream off the heat so it stays smooth.
Fold the cooked rotini into the creamy sauce and portion it out.
